newsitem.title: JAPAN: Casio earnings jump 33 percent for half-year.
newsitem.headline: Casio earnings jump 33 percent for half-year.

text.p: Watch and calculator maker Casio Computer Co. Ltd. said Thursday its half-year earnings leaped 33 percent, helped by booming sales of digital watches.
Casio said its profits jumped to 4.17 billion Japanese yen ($37.2 million) for the six months ended in September from the yeyar-ago level.
The digital watch manufacturer forecast its profit for the full business year ending March 31, 1997 would soar nearly 30 percent to eight billion yen ($71.4 million).
Sales of multi-functional digital watches, which store data such as telephone numbers, and sturdy "G-Shock" watches, popular among younger consumers, contributed to overall sales, it said.

"In the digital watch division, G-shock as well as the Baby-G model for ladies were a great hit both at home and abroad," the company said. Half-year profit from that division alone was up a solid 31.4 percent year-on-year.
